review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not continue this cumulative manuscript through another ordinary revision round. A new, sharply focused paper on verified nonlinear policy construction, or a genuinely method-specific NBO study in a scalable nonlinear economy, could merit evaluation.
blocking_findings: The nonlinear full-policy certificate is centered on a verified spline Bellman construction; the trained ReLU network proposes actions but is not independently certified through its own Bellman residual chain.

The precision-adaptation mechanism is not exercised: all 1,530 adaptive updates use binary32, with no binary64 update or rejected precision attempt, and all 48 tuned services select fixed32 on their first trial.
Structural control is faster than the best factor method in all sixteen quadratic policy objects, and adaptive precision has no stable timing advantage over fixed64.
The spline method is faster and has a smaller global policy bound in all four nonlinear economies; the neural cost interval is strictly better in none of the sixteen displayed same-economy cells.
The nonquadratic execution remains one-dimensional, grid-first, finite-shock and four-period, so it does not establish scalable nonlinear NBO performance.
The price-four economic gain is relative to retaining a stale price-one rule and is also obtained by the conventional spline policy; it is not method-specific.
The native-arithmetic study leaves deployed feedback evaluation at zero execution allowance and does not close one end-to-end floating implementation contract.
The cumulative platform-level scope remains substantially broader than the two completed constructive realizations and their adverse method comparisons.
positive_findings: R39 is a complete, self-contained and source-bound review snapshot.
The nonlinear residual-oscillation comparison appears internally coherent under its stated assumptions and compares all feasible adapted policies.
The constructive spline/ReLU fallback and all-state breakpoint verifier are explicit and reproducible.
The complete-step residual proposition covers the correct native matrix error object rather than only final storage rounding.
The factorial removes the old inverse-caching confound at the design level and retains failed warm gates.
The investment-cost counterfactual has a clear mechanical-exposure and reoptimization decomposition.
Unfavorable structural and spline comparisons, source chronology and original clocks are preserved.

limitations: The reviewer did not rerun or retime the original 315 economic services; their committed clocks are treated as frozen observations.
The reviewer verified the committed records and central new algebra, not every line of every inherited theorem and application.
Three timing repetitions per deterministic object do not support population or hardware-general performance inference.
Strict neural-versus-spline ordering is claimed only when the reported policy-value intervals are disjoint.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
